title: MintReceipt
description: The AUDIT RECORD of a mint transaction (roadmap Phase 5.2 additive path; 5.4b new path) — the EXECUTION half of prose→fact evolution, the moment the system crosses the ADR-009 human-authority boundary. A FactCandidatePlan (fact-candidate-plan.schema.json) stages candidates for review; mint is the distinct, human-authorized action that promotes ACCEPTED candidates into registry/facts/ — the first and only fact-writing operation in the system. This receipt records exactly what a single mint did, so an irreversible SSOT change is never silent: which plan authorized it, which candidates a human accepted, each entity's fact_version transition, and the registry-version transition. Mint applies two candidate classes: `additive` (fill an empty field on an existing entity + bump fact_version — the monotone-safe subset that never overwrites a declared fact and needs no new id) and, since 5.4b, `new` (establish a brand-new entity BY NAME: an id is allocated through the append-only ID Mint Ledger, a minimal fact record is written, fact_version goes 0→1). The `new` path is deliberately narrow this phase: it mints only a name-establishing candidate whose target_type resolves to exactly one type_code and whose new-fact requirements are satisfiable from {id,name,fact_version,status} (Character/Item); an ambiguous type (WorldRule→MAG|TEC), a structured-required type (Event/Timeline/Relationship), or a non-name field on a not-yet-existent entity is REFUSED, not guessed. `conflicting` candidates (a retcon overwrite — the highest-risk SSOT operation) remain out of scope and MUST be refused. The mint is validate-then-write: the post-mint registry is validated in memory against the full deterministic gate and committed ONLY if it passes (a mint that would introduce a dangling ref, a tombstone ref, or a causality cycle is rejected and writes nothing). A plan that has gone STALE (a pinned fact advanced since reconciliation) MUST be refused. Two structural invariants: `authority` const human — mint is the authorized crossing itself, so the receipt records the human authorization, it is never auto-issued; and `gating` const false — a receipt is an audit record, it does not gate a build (ADR-003). Written to registry/derived/mint-receipts/, NEVER to registry/facts/ (a receipt is not a story fact, ADR-006).

authority.description: Structural invariant (ADR-009): minting into the SSOT is an irreversible transition only a human authorizes. The receipt records that authorization; it is never issued by an automatic step.

gating.description: Structural invariant (ADR-003): a mint receipt is an audit record, not a build gate.

authorized.description: The explicit human authorization that crossed the boundary. Its presence is what distinguishes a committed mint from a preview (which writes nothing and issues no receipt).

confirmed.description: A committed receipt only exists when a human confirmed the mint (CLI --confirm). A preview never produces a receipt.

actor.description: Optional record of who authorized (operator id / name).

accepted_candidates.description: The candidate ids (CAND-*) the human accepted from the plan. Only these were considered for minting; everything else in the plan was left untouched.

source_plan.description: The FactCandidatePlan this mint executed. Pinning it makes the mint auditable back to the exact reconciliation (and its prose source).

plan_content_hash.description: The plan's content_hash at mint time (sha256:...).

chapter_draft_id.description: The prose the plan's candidates ultimately came from (carried through for audit).

registry_version.description: The monotone registry version transition this mint caused. A mint that writes any fact bumps the registry version once.

minted.description: One entry per fact written. An `additive` entry filled an empty field on an existing entity and bumped its fact_version; a `new` entry (5.4b) established a brand-new entity by name at a ledger-allocated id, with fact_version 0→1.

entity_id.description: The fact the value was written to: an existing entity (additive) or the newly ledger-minted id (new).

classification.description: Which mintable class this entry applied. `additive`: fill an empty field on an existing entity. `new`: establish a brand-new entity by name at a minted id. `conflicting`/`consistent`/`unverifiable` are refused before commit, so they never appear here.

type_code.description: Present on a `new` entry: the frozen type code the minted id belongs to (CHR/ITM/…), resolved from the candidate's target_type. Absent on `additive` (the entity already exists).

field.description: The (possibly dotted) fact field that was filled. For a `new` entry this is the name-establishing field (`name`).

before.description: 0 for a `new` entity (it did not exist); the prior version for `additive`.

revalidation.description: The post-mint deterministic re-gate result. The mint committed only because this passed; recorded for audit.

checks.description: The gate checks the post-mint registry was validated against.

rationale.description: Human-readable summary of what was minted.
